# AAC weekly updates

Each week this folder gets one page listing the features and fixes merged to `main` in the last seven days. It is written for people who have the proof of concept installed and want to know what changed before they update.

## How to get the update

| You want | Do this |
|---|---|
| An e-mail each week | The maintainers send the update by e-mail to people who run the proof of concept. To be added or removed, ask the AAC contact you work with. Do not post an e-mail address in an issue: issues are public. |
| To read it when you choose | Open the newest page in the list above. |
| Every change, in full | Read [CHANGELOG.md](../../CHANGELOG.md). |

The e-mail and the page in this folder carry the same text.

## What an update contains

- **Needs action when you update**: changes marked as breaking. Read these first.
- **New**: features.
- **Fixed**: defects corrected, including results that were wrong before.
- **Policy library**: moves of the pinned Rego policy library, which can change what a control reports.
- **Install and documentation**, **Maintenance**, **Dependency updates**.

Each line links to its pull request. A line here is a title; the changelog entry says what to do about it.

## Ask for a feature or a change

[Open a request](https://github.com/Ansible-Automated-Compliance/aac/issues/new/choose). There are forms for a new feature, a change to how something works, a report you need, and a problem. Requests are public, so leave out host names, addresses, tenant names and anything else that identifies your environment.

## For maintainers

```bash
python3 scripts/weekly_update.py --email ~/Downloads   # the seven days ending today (UTC)
python3 scripts/weekly_update.py --stdout              # preview only
```

The script reads merged pull requests with the GitHub CLI, writes `docs/updates/<date>.md`, refreshes the list above and, with `--email`, writes `AAC-weekly-update-<date>.html`: the same text as an HTML note with inline styles and full links. Open that file in a browser, select all, copy and paste it into the message (or use it as the HTML body); the subject is the first line. Send to the list as blind copy. Merge the page in this folder through a pull request so the public record matches what was sent.

Pull request titles are the update, so write them for a reader who runs AAC: `feat(scope): what they get`, `fix(scope): what was wrong`. A `!` after the type (`feat!:`) puts the line under "Needs action when you update".
